# Serialization errors and warnings

Diagnostics about converting compile-time values into run-time code, and about the serialization of aspects and fabrics across projects.

| Article | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| <xref:lama0200> | A compile-time value whose type can't be converted to run-time code is used where a run-time value is expected. |
| <xref:lama0201> | A compile-time value converted to run-time code contains a cyclic reference or is nested too deeply. |
| <xref:lama0202> | A compile-time multidimensional array is converted to a run-time value. |
| <xref:lama0203> | A compile-time dictionary with a custom equality comparer is converted to a run-time value. |
| <xref:lama0204> | A serializable base type from a referenced project has no constructor that the generated serializer can call. |
| <xref:lama0205> | A serializable type derives from a non-serializable base type that has no parameterless constructor. |
| <xref:lama0207> | The manual serializer of a base type has no parameterless constructor, so the serializers of derived types can't derive from it. |
| <xref:lama0208> | A compile-time serializable type declares more than one nested serializer. |
| <xref:lama0209> | The base type of a compile-time serializable type declares more than one nested serializer. |
| <xref:lama0210> | Metalama can't generate a serializer for a positional record that implements ICompileTimeSerializable. |
